name: Sirius Satellite Radio (Tundra)
best_known_for: Only commercial fleet using the 24-hour Tundra orbit — three satellites at 63.4° critical inclination, each dwelling ~16 hours per day over North America
credit: Sirius Satellite Radio launched FM-1 from Baikonur on 2000-06-30 atop a Proton-K. The Tundra orbit (24-hour period, ~25,000 × 35,786 km) at the 63.4° critical inclination keeps each satellite high in the sky over CONUS for two-thirds of every orbit, giving handhelds in urban canyons the elevation angles a geostationary signal can't match. Merged with XM Radio in 2008 to form Sirius XM.
